clue.text: Seaside attraction in which you could find top local brew,OK?

indicators.note: the letters of the following words can be found, rearranged, within the attraction's name

explanation.surface: An advert for a resort landmark that promises a decent local beer inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in which you could find' says the letters of TOP LOCAL BREW OK are all there, shuffled. Blackpool Tower is the Eiffel-style landmark on the seafront at Blackpool, a resort in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous tower on Blackpool's promenade is a classic British seafront tourist draw.

clue.text: Stars in Hollywood, etc? Sure thing — ace!

parts.note: Hollywood is part of Los Angeles, abbreviated LA
a cert is British slang for a certainty, especially a racing tip
A is the abbreviation for ace on playing cards

explanation.surface: Hollywood's stars are apparently a sure-fire success.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stars' looks like film actors in Hollywood, but it means a constellation; Lacerta, the Lizard, is a small northern one.
explanation.definitionFit: This constellation is a named group of stars in the northern sky.

clue.text: Gosh, it's a particular hormone used in medicine!

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise, much like gosh
'tis is the old poetic contraction of it is
one, as in 'one Mr Jones', singles out a particular individual

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims in surprise at a specific hormone their doctor prescribes.
explanation.walkthrough: COR is everyday British slang for surprise, as in 'cor blimey'.
explanation.definitionFit: This steroid from the adrenal gland is given as an anti-inflammatory drug, so it is a hormone used medically.

clue.text: Scientist in setup, a scallywag

indicators.note: the scientist's name sits inside the run of letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A scientist turns out to be a rogue within some organisation.
explanation.walkthrough: The name runs across setuP A SCALlywag; Blaise Pascal was the French mathematician and physicist.
explanation.definitionFit: Blaise Pascal was a seventeenth-century French physicist and mathematician, remembered in the unit of pressure.

clue.text: Item of food is old scrap, dry inside

indicators.note: the word for dry is placed within the word for scrap

parts.note: a scrap is a fight, and a melee is a confused brawl
TT, teetotal, describes someone who is dry, not drinking alcohol

explanation.surface: Some food is dismissed as an old leftover, with something dry in the middle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scrap' looks like a leftover morsel of food, but here it is a fight; 'inside' places the dry letters in the middle of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A dish of beaten eggs cooked flat in a pan is a food item.

clue.text: Consternation — little girl's lost hair

indicators.note: the girl's name has been lost, taken away from the longer word

parts.note: consternation is anxiety or dismay, which is distress
Di is a short form of the girl's name Diana

explanation.surface: A little girl is distraught at having lost some hair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'girl's lost' reads 'girl has lost': DI comes out of DISTRESS.
explanation.definitionFit: A long lock or curl of someone's hair, often in poetry.

clue.text: Wife has right viewpoint in dispute

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for wife in genealogy
an angle is a point of view, a slant on a story

explanation.surface: A wife insists on her own point of view during a row.
explanation.definitionFit: To argue noisily or at length is to quarrel or squabble.

clue.text: Take back deserter on run, possibly to have time inside

indicators.note: the abbreviation for time goes within the rearranged letters
possibly signals that these letters may be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A deserter on the run is caught and may face doing time in prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges DESERTER ON RUN and 'to have time inside' puts T among those letters. The phrase is printed on undeliverable mail, and was an Elvis song.
explanation.definitionFit: Mail marked this way is refused and goes back to its writer, so the phrase means take or send back.

clue.text: Actor cries — dole spurious, as these are shed

definitions.text: Actor cries — dole spurious, as these are shed

indicators.note: spurious means false, so these letters come out in a false order

explanation.surface: An actor weeps on cue, handing out fake tears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spurious' rearranges ACTOR CRIES DOLE; the whole clue also describes the answer, an actor's false weeping.
explanation.definitionFit: False shows of sorrow, named after the belief that the reptile weeps while eating its prey.

clue.text: Files of left-wing society probed by Conservative men

indicators.note: to be probed is to have something pushed into you, so the later letters go inside

parts.note: a red is a left-winger, a communist
OR, other ranks, means the ordinary soldiers or men

explanation.surface: Security services examine the files of a communist group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'probed by' puts the Conservative and the men inside the left-wing society, splitting it after its second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Files are stored documents, which is what records are.

clue.text: Smart English worker that's kept on

parts.note: in cricket the on side is also called the leg side
the worker ant is a classic crossword worker

explanation.surface: A smart English employee is retained in their job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kept on' looks like staying employed, but 'on' gives LEG, the cricket term for the on side; 'that's kept' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Smart in the sense of stylish and well dressed, graceful in appearance.

clue.text: Paintings, etc, left in box in tissue

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'Paintings, etc, left in box in tissue' lacks the I the answer needs (ART+I+L in CAGE); the setter confirmed on Times for the Times that 'I' before 'left' was dropped in print
annotationWithheld.clue: Paintings, etc, left in box in tissue

clue.text: Tease American about showing flattery

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the joined words are read backwards

parts.note: to rag someone is to tease them

explanation.surface: Someone teases an American for laying on the compliments too thickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns the tease and the American round together, not each on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweet talk is flattery, the sweetness used to make it more palatable.

clue.text: Monster to continue in boring fashion?

definitions.meaning: a winged fire-breathing creature of legend
to go on tediously, the way a long speech does

explanation.surface: A monster that goes on and on, boring everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: A fire-breathing legendary beast; and as two words, to drag out tediously, like a dull meeting.

clue.text: Rough walk starts with nettles and thorns

parts.note: to stride is to walk with long steps

indicators.note: the starts of the next two words are taken, their first letters

explanation.surface: A rough walk through nettles and thorns.
explanation.definitionFit: Rough here means harsh and grating, as a loud unpleasant sound is.

clue.text: He could pour out oration to ensnare a maiden, maybe

definitions.text: He could pour out oration to ensnare a maiden, maybe

indicators.note: to ensnare is to trap, so the rearranged letters close round the others
letters poured out are spilled and land in a new order

parts.note: M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A suitor delivers a flowery speech to win over a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pour out' rearranges ORATION and 'to ensnare' wraps it round A+M; the whole clue pictures the lover himself.
explanation.definitionFit: This Italian word names a male lover or admirer, who might well woo a girl with speeches.

clue.text: Criticises what NI county boss does?

definitions.meaning: a boss manages things, and Down is a county of Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: A complaint about the head of a Northern Irish county council.
explanation.walkthrough: NI is Northern Ireland, one of whose six counties is Down.
explanation.definitionFit: To disparage someone; and literally what the head of County Down does, managing it.

clue.text: Philosopher joins Ulster party? Should be put away!

parts.note: John Locke was the English empiricist philosopher
the DUP is the Democratic Unionist Party of Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: A thinker joins a Northern Ireland party and someone says he should be jailed.
explanation.walkthrough: Ulster is often used for Northern Ireland; its Democratic Unionist Party is the DUP.
explanation.definitionFit: To put someone away is to imprison them.

clue.text: Eleven, having a game in American city

parts.note: Eleven points to the answer at 11 across, which means smart, so stylish
Go is the Japanese board game played with stones

explanation.surface: A football eleven plays a match in an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eleven' looks like a team, but it refers to 11 across, whose answer, meaning stylish, gives CHIC.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest city in Illinois, on Lake Michigan, is a major American metropolis.

clue.text: Man offering brandy to you and me

parts.note: marc is a brandy distilled from grape pulp
us is the pronoun for you and me together

explanation.surface: A man offers to share his brandy.
explanation.definitionFit: A man's first name, as in the Roman Mark Antony.

clue.text: Victor would carry this plant around hospital

indicators.note: the victor's word holds the answer inside it, so take away what it carries
the winner's word is this plant wrapped around the hospital letter

parts.note: a victor is a winner, a champion
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A winner carrying a plant around a hospital ward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'would carry this ... around hospital' says CHAMPION is the answer wrapped round H; take out H to get the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A pink or white wild flower of hedgerows, related to the pinks.

clue.text: In spring, the woman's becoming a mountaineer, maybe

indicators.note: the woman's word sits in the word for spring

parts.note: a spa is a mineral spring
her is the possessive for the woman's

explanation.surface: In springtime a woman takes up climbing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spring' looks like the season, but it is a water source, SPA.
explanation.definitionFit: A Himalayan people famous as guides and porters on climbing expeditions, so mountaineers by example.

clue.text: One who wanted more wind

definitions.meaning: Oliver, the workhouse boy in Dickens, asked for more gruel
to wind is to coil or turn, rhyming with kind

explanation.surface: A gust of wind that never seems satisfied.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickens's orphan Oliver famously asked for more; and to wind is to coil or turn round.

clue.text: Vagrant male put in prison

indicators.note: the male letter is placed inside the word for prison

parts.note: a trap confines whatever it catches, a kind of prison

explanation.surface: A homeless man is sent to jail.
explanation.definitionFit: A tramp is a homeless wanderer, a vagabond.

clue.text: Rugby players, perhaps — academic types, too

definitions.meaning: pupils of Rugby, the English public school where the game began
medieval university scholars who taught scholastic philosophy

explanation.surface: Rugby players turn out to be scholars as well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rugby players' suggests the sport, but here it is Rugby School in Warwickshire and its pupils.
explanation.definitionFit: Boys educated at Rugby, the English public school, are its pupils; medieval scholastic philosophers were also called this.

clue.text: Indians taking soldiers back to a house

indicators.note: back means the word for soldiers is read in reverse

parts.note: a para is a paratrooper, a soldier

explanation.surface: Native Americans take some soldiers back to a house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses only the soldiers, which then precede A and the house abbreviation. Paras are British paratroopers.
explanation.definitionFit: A Native American people of the Great Plains, once called Indians.

clue.text: Acquire through a combination of ire and zeal

indicators.note: combining the two words' letters produces a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone gains their goal by mixing anger with enthusiasm.
explanation.definitionFit: To realize a sum is to gain it, as from a sale.

clue.text: Old bob, travelling on a fixed route and looking for the best bargain

parts.note: bob was slang for a shilling, the old British coin abbreviated S
hopping, as in island-hopping, is travelling from place to place
a round is a regular route, like a postman's

explanation.surface: Someone takes a bus on a set route to hunt for the best deals.
explanation.walkthrough: A shilling, nicknamed a bob, was a pre-1971 British coin, abbreviated S.
explanation.definitionFit: Comparing prices in different shops to find a good deal.
